featureRef: 5.6 Barcode, ID-card or QR attendance scanning
name: Mark staff attendance by card scan, with a code-verified route when the card is not to hand
priorityReason: It removes the daily manual marking that determines pay, and closes the gap where somebody is marked present in their absence.

goal.capability: to mark my own arrival by scanning my card, and to be marked by code when I have forgotten it
goal.outcome: my attendance is recorded by my own act, and nobody can record it for me while I am not there

secondaryActors.involvement: Scan their own cards on the same terms.
Marks a staff member manually when the card is forgotten, and can only do so against a verified code.
Uses the resulting attendance for payroll and cannot amend it.

externalActors.involvement: Delivers the one-time code to the number on the staff record.

additional.description: A card is scanned at the reader on arrival.
A staff member has no scan by the configured time and the office begins a manual mark.

preconditions.condition: The staff member holds a card or code linked to their record (BR-2).
The staff record carries a contact number, since the code is sent to it (BR-5).
For a manual mark, an authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin.
The date is a working day.

postConditions: The staff member's attendance is recorded with the time of the scan, and the record shows it was scanned.
Where the card was forgotten, the record shows it was marked manually and verified by code rather than scanned, so the two are never confused.
No manual mark exists without a matching code, so nobody has been marked present in their absence.
The code that was used is spent and cannot mark a second day.
The attendance flows into the staff attendance record and from there into payroll.
A scan on a day the school is closed was refused, so a closed day carries no attendance.
Where the code never arrived, the resend was logged, so a pattern of resends against one person is visible.
This route was used for staff only. No student attendance was marked by scanning.

businessRules.rule: This route is for staff only. Student attendance is never marked by scanning, whatever the card can do.
Each staff member holds a card or code linked to their record. The card carries its own identifier rather than the staff ID, so a card can be replaced without changing the person.
The scan time comes from the reader and is never typed. A time somebody entered is not evidence of when they arrived.
A staff member scans their own card. Scanning somebody else's card is the failure this whole design exists to prevent.
Where the card is forgotten, the School Admin starts a manual mark and the system sends a one-time code to the number held on that staff record. The admin does not choose the number.
The code is valid for a configured period and can be used once. A code from yesterday cannot mark today.
A manual mark cannot be made without a matching code. This is the rule that stops anybody being marked present in their absence, and there is no override to it.
The record shows whether the attendance was scanned or marked manually and verified by code. The two are distinguishable for good, so a pattern of manual marks is visible.
Where the code does not arrive the admin may resend it. The staff member is still the only person who can supply it.
Every code sent and every resend is logged, so repeated resends against one person can be seen rather than inferred.
The attendance produced here is the same staff attendance record as a manual entry. It carries the same codes and feeds the same payroll calculation.
No attendance is recorded on a day the school is closed, whether scanned or marked manually.
A lost or replaced card is deactivated so the old identifier stops working. A card that keeps working after it is lost is a card anybody can use.

transitions.condition: The staff member supplies the code and it matches (BR-7).

basicFlow.userAction: Issues each staff member a card or code linked to their record.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Links the card identifier to the staff record without exposing the staff ID on it.

basicFlow.navigation: Arrives at the entrance → Scan point
basicFlow.systemResponse: Resolves the card to the staff member, records the attendance and the time from the reader, and marks the source as Scanned.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Attendance → Today's scans → Start manual mark
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the record of a staff member who has forgotten their card.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Confirms no scan exists for the day and prepares the verification.
Sends a one-time code to the number held on that staff record, not to a number the admin supplies.

basicFlow.navigation: Gives the code to the admin
basicFlow.userAction: Reads the code from their own phone and gives it to the admin.

basicFlow.navigation: Manual mark by code → Enter code → Confirm mark
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the code the staff member gave them.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Marks the attendance only where the code matches, and records the source as marked manually and verified by code.
Writes the attendance into the staff attendance record, which feeds payroll in the ordinary way.

alternateFlows.navigation: Manual mark by code → Resend code
alternateFlows.behaviour: The admin resends it. The staff member is still the only person who can supply it, and every resend is logged so a pattern is visible (BR-9, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The card is lost or damaged
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Card → Deactivate card → Issue staff card
alternateFlows.behaviour: The old identifier is deactivated so it stops working, and a new card is issued. A card that keeps working after it is lost is a card anybody can use (BR-13).

alternateFlows.condition: A staff member scans a second time on leaving
alternateFlows.behaviour: The second scan records the time out on the same day's record rather than creating a second attendance.

alternateFlows.condition: The staff member is not actually present
alternateFlows.behaviour: They cannot supply the code, so the mark cannot be made. This is the case the verification exists for (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The reader is out of service
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Today's scans → Start manual mark
alternateFlows.behaviour: Every staff member is marked by the code route. It is slower, and the record shows each mark as manual and verified rather than scanned (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The code has expired before it is entered
alternateFlows.navigation: Manual mark by code → Resend code
alternateFlows.behaviour: A fresh code is sent. An expired code cannot mark the day (BR-6).

outOfScope.item: Student attendance, which is never marked by scanning
The staff attendance record and its corrections

departures.requirement: A scan is acknowledged within 2 seconds, because a queue at the entrance at eight in the morning is why people stop using it.
There is no route anywhere that marks a staff member manually without a matching code. The absence of an override is the control.
Whether attendance was scanned or code-verified is recorded permanently and cannot be changed afterwards.
Where the reader is out of service the code route carries the whole school, so a hardware failure slows the morning rather than stopping it.
Scans, codes and manual marks are retained 7 years, matching payroll records.

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.
